convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to call external 'WeightOscillator' indicator. While the indicator may be a standard MT5 CodeBase indicator, it is not a built-in MT5 indicator, requiring either the indicator .ex5 file or source reproduction for Python conversion. Entry/exit logic appears straightforward otherwise.

other_exits: Opposite signal closes current position before opening new one (signal reversal exit)

custom_logic_notes: The WeightOscillator is a custom indicator accessed via iCustom(). The EA uses the standard Exp template pattern: on each new bar, it reads two buffer values from the custom indicator (likely the oscillator value and its signal/zero line), checks for crossover/crossunder to generate signals, and manages a single position at a time with signal-reversal closing. SL/TP values in inputs are typically in points and require digit-adjustment (multiply by 10) for 5-digit/3-digit brokers, which the template handles via POINT value recalculation.
external_dependencies: WeightOscillator.ex5 (custom indicator required for iCustom call)
python_conversion_notes: The WeightOscillator custom indicator logic must be reproduced in Python. The indicator appears to be a weighted oscillator combining multiple moving average types. Check the MQL5 CodeBase for the WeightOscillator source to replicate its calculation. Once the indicator is ported, the EA logic is straightforward: new-bar crossover of the oscillator value above/below zero triggers long/short entries with fixed SL/TP. Position management is single-position with reversal close. Standard point/pip adjustment for 5-digit brokers must be handled in Python.
